# Operation reference

Every operation takes a JSON request (`doc-control <op> --json '{…}'`, the MCP tool of the same name with `.` as `_`, or `doc_control.api`) and answers with the envelope `{api, ok, op, doc, result, warnings, next}` or an error from [errors.md](errors.md). `doc-control help <op>` prints the full JSON Schema.

## `anchor.create` (read)

Make an anchor (quote with context) for a range, to find the passage again after edits.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx file. |
| `at` | string | yes | Range inside one paragraph, e.g. p142#a7b2a7b2:10-15, or a whole paragraph or sentence (p142#a7b2a7b2.s3). |
| `context` | integer |  | Characters of prefix and of suffix to keep. |

## `anchor.resolve` (read)

Find an anchor's passage now: its range, score and match kind (exact, normalized or fuzzy), or the ambiguous candidates. mode exact never returns a fuzzy match.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx file. |
| `anchor` | object | yes | An anchor from anchor.create, or just {exact, prefix, suffix}. |
| `mode` | `best` \| `exact` |  | best: verbatim matches first, then fuzzy ones (match says which). exact: only places holding the quote verbatim or, when none does, in the normalised text (soft hyphens and zero-width characters ignored, whitespace collapsed, as text.normalized); anything else is ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND. |

## `batch` (write)

Apply text.replace, para.insert, para.delete, para.move, style.apply, format.apply, comment.add, comment.reply and comment.resolve together, all or nothing, or style.create/update/rename/merge together, or revision.accept and revision.reject to resolve revisions (by ids, author, address range or all); dry_run previews.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx (live: or the file name of one open in a live app). |
| `ops` | array | yes | Operations, applied together. Every address refers to the document as read; an operation placed relative to a paragraph another operation deletes or moves is a BATCH_CONFLICT. Kinds: text.replace ['at', 'text']; para.insert ['after', 'before', 'text']; para.delete ['at']; para.move ['after', 'at', 'before']; style.apply ['at', 'style']; format.apply ['align', 'at', 'bold', 'font', 'indent_first_line_cm', 'indent_left_cm', 'indent_right_cm', 'italic', 'line_spacing', 'size_pt', 'small_caps', 'spacing_after_pt', 'spacing_before_pt', 'underline']; comment.add ['at', 'text']; comment.reply ['comment', 'text']; comment.resolve ['comment', 'resolved']; style.create ['based_on', 'custom', 'default', 'id', 'link', 'name', 'next', 'paragraph', 'quick', 'run', 'type']; style.update ['based_on', 'link', 'next', 'paragraph', 'quick', 'run', 'style']; style.rename ['id', 'name', 'style']; style.merge ['from', 'into']; revision.accept ['all', 'at', 'author', 'ids']; revision.reject ['all', 'at', 'author', 'ids']. |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Preview only; write nothing. |
| `tracked` | boolean |  | Tracked changes (the only mode, true). |
| `author` | string |  | Revision author. |
| `tag` | string |  | Appended to the author. |
| `engine` | `file` \| `live` |  | `live` edits the document open in Word or LibreOffice (see live.open). |

## `capabilities` (read)

API version, engines and the list of operations.

## `comments.list` (read)

Comments in thread order (each root then its replies) with resolved state and location.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `resolved` | boolean |  | Only resolved (true) or open (false). |
| `author` | string |  | Only this author. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `compare` (read)

Write a new redline .docx from two versions: every difference a tracked change; the inputs are never modified.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `old` | string | yes | Path of the earlier version (.docx). |
| `new` | string | yes | Path of the later version (.docx). |
| `output` | string | yes | Path of the redline to create (must not exist). |
| `author` | string |  | Revision author (default Claude). |
| `tag` | string |  | Appended to the author as `author (tag)`. |
| `date` | string |  | Revision date, ISO 8601 with time zone. |

## `diff` (read)

Paragraph alignment between two versions of a document, with a cross-version address map.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `old` | string | yes | Path of the earlier version (.docx). |
| `new` | string | yes | Path of the later version (.docx). |
| `collapse_runs` | boolean |  | List runs of shifted unchanged paragraphs as one record each. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `find` (read)

Find text or a regex; matches come back as paragraph ranges, capped, with a cursor. The first page also gives `total` (or `total_at_least` and `more: true` when the time budget stopped the count). `query_word` is the query as typed in Word's Find box (^p, ^l, ^t, ^s, ^^; null past 255 characters, with ignore_accents or with a soft or no-break hyphen in the query; not for a regex), with `query_word_options` (match_case, whole_words) to tick there.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx file. |
| `query` | string | yes | Text to find (at most 1000 characters), or a Python regex if `regex`. |
| `regex` | boolean |  | Treat `query` as a regex. |
| `ignore_case` | boolean |  | Ignore case. |
| `ignore_accents` | boolean |  | Ignore accents: `maria` finds `María`. A regex must be written without accents then. |
| `whole_word` | boolean |  | Match only whole words (no letter, digit or mark on either side). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most matches to return; more are reached with `cursor`. |
| `context` | integer |  | Characters of surrounding text on each side of a match. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous page. |
| `stories` | array |  | Stories to read (default ["body"]): "notes" adds footnotes and endnotes, each after the paragraph holding its mark; "headers" adds headers and footers, after the body. Their addresses carry a prefix (fn3/p1#…, hdr1.default/p1#…). |

|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | string |  | Operation or batch operation kind. |

## `history.list` (read)

The undo log, newest first: what each write changed, whether it was undone, and the deleted paragraphs `restore` can bring back.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string |  | Path to the .docx. |
| `store` | string |  | A store folder (see history.orphans) to read instead of the document's own. |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` of the previous response. |
| `kind` | `batch` \| `restore` \| `undo` \| `open` \| `purge` |  |  |

## `history.orphans` (read)

List stores whose document is gone (app-data stores, and `dir`/.doc-control). Their history is never deleted automatically: restore from it with `store`, or purge it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string |  | Also scan this folder. |

## `history.purge` (write)

Remove undo history (all, or before a date) for privacy, leaving a tombstone. Run with dry_run first, then repeat with its `confirm`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string |  | Path to the .docx. |
| `store` | string |  | A store folder (see history.orphans) to read instead of the document's own. |
| `all` | boolean |  | Remove the whole log. |
| `before` | string |  | Remove entries older than this ISO date or time (UTC). |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | List what would go; returns confirm. |
| `confirm` | string |  | From the dry run. |

## `history.search` (read)

Find a quote in the undo log: in the requests, and in the text of every paragraph before and after each write.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string |  | Path to the .docx. |
| `store` | string |  | A store folder (see history.orphans) to read instead of the document's own. |
| `query` | string | yes | Text to find. |
| `ignore_case` | boolean |  |  |
| `ignore_accents` | boolean |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |

## `info` (read)

File facts: size, hash, paragraph count, properties and which parts exist.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |

## `layout.get` (read)

The document's page plan: per section where it starts, its break, page numbering, title page, and the header and footer text per kind (default, first, even), with PAGE, NUMPAGES and chapter (STYLEREF) fields as {PAGE}, {NUMPAGES} and {chapter}. A kind the section does not define is null (inherited). The plan carries "version": 1.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |

## `live.close` (write)

Close the open document; with unsaved changes it needs `save` or `discard`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the document, or the file name of one open in a live app. |
| `engine` | `live` |  | Always the live engine; may be left out. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save, then close. |
| `discard` | boolean |  | Close and drop the unsaved changes. |

## `live.open` (write)

Attach to the app window holding the document, or open it in a live app.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the document, or the file name of one open in a live app. |
| `engine` | `live` |  | Always the live engine; may be left out. |
| `app` | string |  | `word` or `libreoffice`. |
| `front` | boolean |  | Bring the app's window to the front (default true); the reply's `front` says whether it came. |

## `live.save` (write)

Save the open document in its app.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the document, or the file name of one open in a live app. |
| `engine` | `live` |  | Always the live engine; may be left out. |

## `live.select` (write)

Select a paragraph in the app's window, by address (`at`) or by a `locate` find phrase, and return its text and address.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the document, or the file name of one open in a live app. |
| `engine` | `live` |  | Always the live engine; may be left out. |
| `at` | string |  | Paragraph address, e.g. `p142#a7b2a7b2`. |
| `find_phrase` | string |  | A phrase that occurs once in the document (`\r` for a paragraph mark), as `locate` gives it. |
| `find_phrase_across` | `previous` \| `next` \| `both` |  | `locate`'s `find_phrase_across`, for a phrase spanning a mark. |
| `mode` | `select` \| `cursor` |  | `select` (default) selects the paragraph; `cursor` only puts the cursor at its start, so typing or Delete cannot replace it. |
| `front` | boolean |  | Bring the app's window to the front (default true); the reply's `front` says whether it came. |
| `paragraphs_after` | integer |  | Select the paragraph this many after the one named. |

## `live.selection` (read)

The text selected in the app's window, and the paragraph the cursor is in.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the document, or the file name of one open in a live app. |
| `engine` | `live` |  | Always the live engine; may be left out. |

## `live.status` (read)

Live apps (Word, LibreOffice) found and reachable, and the documents they have open; with `doc`, which app has it open, its full path, and whether it has unsaved changes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string |  | Path to the document, or the file name of one open in a live app. |
| `engine` | `live` |  | Always the live engine; may be left out. |

## `locate` (read)

Chapter, scene, estimated page and the shortest unique first-and-last-words phrase of each paragraph, plus a phrase Word's Find meets once (one, a range, or the whole document, paged).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `at` | string |  | Paragraph address or range (offsets ignored), e.g. p142#a7b2a7b2; default the whole document (empty paragraphs left out). |
| `overrides` | array |  | Force or deny a chapter or scene at paragraphs by fingerprint. |
| `profile` | object |  | Detection settings for this document. |
| `structure` | boolean |  | false: skip chapter, part and scene detection (they come back null), for callers that keep their own structure; faster on a single paragraph. Default true. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `note.add` (write)

Add a footnote or endnote at a body offset: the reference mark and the note text are both tracked insertions, so rejecting them removes the note. Creates the notes part when the document has none. Returns the note's id, displayed number and address.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `at` | string | yes | Body point p3#fp:10-10 (the mark goes after the offset), a range inside one paragraph (after it) or a paragraph (at its end). |
| `kind` | `footnote` \| `endnote` | yes |  |
| `text` | string | yes | The note text, one line. |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Preview only; write nothing. |
| `author` | string |  | Revision author. |
| `tag` | string |  | Appended to the author. |

## `open` (write)

Back up the document into its store (retention applies) and note it in the history; call it when a session starts. The document is not changed.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |

The headings of the document with level, style and address, in order.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `stories` | array |  | Stories to read (default ["body"]): "notes" adds footnotes and endnotes, each after the paragraph holding its mark; "headers" adds headers and footers, after the body. Their addresses carry a prefix (fn3/p1#…, hdr1.default/p1#…). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `page.estimate` (read)

Estimated page of each paragraph (or of one): rendered page marks and explicit breaks first, a word-count model otherwise. Always `estimated: true`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `at` | string |  | Only this paragraph, by address, e.g. p142#a7b2a7b2. |
| `by` | `paragraph` \| `page` |  | List one row per paragraph (default) or per page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `para.get` (read)

One paragraph by address: text, style, direct formatting and formatted spans, and layout facts (heading_level is null for a body paragraph, 1-9 for a heading).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `at` | string | yes | Paragraph address from a read result, e.g. p142#a7b2a7b2. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most characters of text to return. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `paragraphs.list` (read)

Every paragraph with its address, text, style and layout facts (optionally the normalised text and the estimated page), in document order. heading_level is null for a body paragraph.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `normalized` | boolean |  | Add `normalized`, the text as `text.normalized` gives it. |
| `pages` | boolean |  | Add the estimated `page` and `page_label` per paragraph, and `page_basis`, `rendered_marks` and `page_count` (see page.estimate). |
| `stories` | array |  | Stories to read (default ["body"]): "notes" adds footnotes and endnotes, each after the paragraph holding its mark; "headers" adds headers and footers, after the body. Their addresses carry a prefix (fn3/p1#…, hdr1.default/p1#…). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `recipe.list` (read)

List the bundled and user recipes, and any recipe files that are invalid.

## `recipe.run` (write)

Run a recipe and return a batch proposal (repeated until stable); apply it with batch.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx file. |
| `recipe` | string |  | Name from recipe.list. |
| `definition` | object |  | An inline declarative recipe (same schema as a stored one). |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Accepted for symmetry; recipe.run never writes. |

## `restore` (write)

Bring a logged paragraph back as a tracked insertion after the paragraph that holds its place now. Without `change`, every paragraph the op deleted.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `store` | string |  | A store folder (see history.orphans) to read instead of the document's own. |
| `op_id` | string | yes | The logged op the paragraph was changed by. |
| `change` | integer |  | Index of one change of the op (history.list shows them). |
| `after` | string |  | Insert after this paragraph address instead of the old place (needed when that place was edited, or the history comes from `store`). |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Preview only; write nothing. |
| `author` | string |  | Revision author. |
| `tag` | string |  | Appended to the author. |

Tracked changes in document order with author, date, type, text and paragraph address.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `author` | string |  | Only this author. |
| `type` | `cell_delete` \| `cell_insert` \| `cell_merge` \| `delete` \| `format` \| `insert` \| `mark_delete` \| `mark_format` \| `mark_insert` \| `mark_move_from` \| `mark_move_to` \| `move_from` \| `move_to` \| `paragraph_format` \| `row_delete` \| `row_insert` |  | Only this type. |
| `stories` | array |  | Stories to list (default ["body"]): "notes" adds footnotes and endnotes, "headers" headers and footers, after the body's revisions; their addresses carry a prefix (fn3/p1#…, hdr1.default/p1#…). Row and cell revisions are listed for the body's tables only. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

| `name` | string |  | Set name. |
| `styles` | array |  | Only these styles (ids or names). |
| `custom_only` | boolean |  | Only user-defined styles. |
| `out` | string |  | Also write the JSON here. |

## `styleset.export-dotx` (write)

Write the document's styles as a new .dotx template; never touches the document.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `out` | string | yes | New .dotx to create. |
| `name` | string |  | Set name. |
| `styles` | array |  | Only these styles (ids or names). |
| `custom_only` | boolean |  | Only user-defined styles. |

## `styleset.import-dotx` (write)

Install the styles of a .dotx template into the document: new styles are added, existing ones replaced (or skipped); dry_run previews.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `path` | string | yes | The .dotx to read. |
| `on_conflict` | `replace` \| `skip` \| `error` |  | A style id already in the document (default replace). |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Preview only; write nothing. |

## `styleset.install` (write)

Install a JSON style set into the document: new styles are added, existing ones replaced (or skipped); dry_run previews.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `styleset` | object |  | The style set (inline). |
| `path` | string |  | Or a style set file. |
| `on_conflict` | `replace` \| `skip` \| `error` |  | A style id already in the document (default replace). |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Preview only; write nothing. |

## `table.get` (read)

One table's grid: its rows of cells, each with its first grid column (`col`), `span` (w:gridSpan), `vmerge` (null, "restart" or "continue") and the addresses of its own paragraphs. A nested table is a table of its own, numbered after the one holding it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `table` | integer |  | Table number, 1-based in document order (the `cell.table` of a paragraph row); text-box and DrawingML tables are not counted. |
| `at` | string |  | Instead of `table`: any paragraph address in the table. |

## `term.rename` (write)

Rename a term everywhere as one tracked batch: whole word, case, preserve case and inflections; dry_run previews with counts.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `from` | string | yes | Term to rename. |
| `to` | string | yes | New term. |
| `whole_word` | boolean |  | Whole words only. |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean |  | Exact spelling only; `to` is used as written. |
| `preserve_case` | boolean |  | LUCÍA becomes ELENA, lucía becomes elena, Lucía becomes Elena. |
| `ignore_accents` | boolean |  | `Lucia` also matches `Lucía`. |
| `inflections` | array |  | Suffixes that follow the term: "s" renames Lucías to Elenas; {"from": "o", "to": "a"} renames Lucíao to Elenaa. |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Plan and preview only; write nothing. |
| `preview_limit` | integer |  | Most changes echoed back in `preview`. |
| `author` | string |  | Revision author. |
| `tag` | string |  | Appended to the author. |

## `text.normalized` (read)

Normalised text (NFC, soft hyphens and zero-width characters removed, whitespace collapsed) with a two-way offset map to the original code points, for a document (whole, or the paragraph/range `at`) or for a `text` string.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string |  | Path to a .docx. |
| `text` | string |  | Text to normalise instead of `doc`. |
| `at` | string |  | Paragraph address or range, e.g. p142#a7b2a7b2:10-15. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most items to return; a response is also capped at about 8,000 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next` value of the previous response, to continue the list. |

## `undo` (write)

Take back a logged batch or restore (the latest one that is still in effect by default), returning its paragraphs to their prior state. Refused if they were edited since.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | yes | Path to the .docx. |
| `op_id` | string |  | The op to undo (default: the latest in effect). |
| `expect` | object |  |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Check and preview; write nothing. |
